text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Alright. Craig.
A: Claire. Hi.
B: Hi.
A: So, where are you?
B: Swindon.
A: Okay. I'm in Faversham, Kent. Have you been?
B: No. Don't think so.
A: No, most people haven't. It's nice. Small. Lots of pubs. Erm, what do you do, Craig?
B: Quality inspection. Engineering firm. Measuring parts, basically.
A: Measuring parts. Measuring them for what, though? Sorry, I genuinely don't know what that involves.
B: Er, so we machine aluminium parts, for other companies, and I put them on the CMM, it's a coordinate measuring machine, it probes the part and tells you if every dimension's in tolerance. Like, if the drawing says a hole's ten mil, plus or minus a couple of microns, it checks it is. Then I write it up.
A: Microns. God. That's quite satisfying, actually, isn't it? Either it's right or it isn't.
B: Yeah, sort of. Mostly. Sometimes it's borderline and the manager wants it out the door anyway.
A: And do you let it go?
B: Er, yeah, usually. If it's that close. Not my call, to be fair.
A: Hm. I'd be awful at that. I'm in interior design, and I'd never be allowed near anything measured in microns. I eyeball everything. My business partner measures things twice and then measures my measurements.
B: Fair enough.
A: Do you enjoy it?
B: It's alright. Pays okay. I'd want the next grade up, though. Quality engineer. Better money.
A: That's a very honest answer. Most people would say they're passionate about it.
B: Not really passionate. It's a job, yeah.
A: No, I respect that. What do you do when you're not measuring?
B: Gym. Bit of gaming. Cars, mostly. Got an A3, I keep it clean.
A: I don't know anything about cars. Mine's a Volvo full of dog hair and crisp packets. My son would probably love you, he's fifteen, all he talks about is cars and football.
B: Who does he support?
A: Arsenal, I think. Or he did. He has it on constantly and I find it unbearably boring, I'm sorry.
B: [laughs] That's alright. I support Swindon. Most people find that boring.
A: Are they any good?
B: No. Lost again Saturday.
A: [laughs] Well, at least you're loyal. Why do you keep going?
B: Er, I go with my dad. Few times a season. It's more that, really. He's got bad knees now, so...
A: That's nice, actually. That's a proper reason. I'll stop being snooty about football, then. Sort of. Did you do that puzzle at the start, by the—
